meta.name: Anthropic
meta.method: Levels are inferred only from Anthropic's own public documents. This is an indicative benchmark of what a mature AI provider publicly evidences, not an audit or certification of Anthropic.

GOV-1.evidence: Accredited ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification (Schellman) covers an AI management system with established roles and oversight; an independent Long-Term Benefit Trust elects part of the board. No named risk owner is published.

GOV-2.evidence: A published, dated Usage Policy sets prohibited uses and high-risk use requirements, enforced by a Safeguards team. Enforcement data for Jan to Jun 2026 reports 11.4 million banned accounts. Staff acknowledgement and yearly review are not evidenced.

RISK-1.evidence: The RSP sets capability assessments on a set interval and published Risk Reports every 3 to 6 months (Feb and Aug 2026). Each model release has a system card recording safety evaluations and deployment decisions.

RISK-2.evidence: Risk Reports cover AI-specific threat models (CBRN uplift, automated AI R&D, sabotage), active mitigations and an overall risk assessment on a 3 to 6 month cycle; ISO 42001 certification attests to a risk assessment and treatment process.

DATA-1.evidence: Commercial terms state Anthropic may not train models on customer content; consumer data has published retention limits (deleted chats purged from back end within 30 days). No attestation specific to data minimisation was found.

ACCESS-1.evidence: Claude Code cloud sessions keep GitHub credentials out of the VM, giving it only a short-lived session-scoped credential via a proxy. Internally, no person has persistent production access (two-party control). No measured leak rate is published.

ACCESS-2.evidence: Claude Code enforces deny, then ask, then allow rule precedence; deny rules cannot be overridden by allow rules or hooks and can be locked in managed settings. Rejections can be logged via opt-in telemetry; no published test evidence.

ROBUST-1.evidence: Anthropic publishes measured prompt injection results: an adaptive attacker with 100 attempts per environment reached 1.4% attack success on Claude Opus 4.5 with safeguards. Classifiers scan untrusted content; red teaming is continuous.

OVERSIGHT-1.evidence: Claude's constitution makes not undermining human oversight its top priority. Claude Code permission modes require approval for sensitive actions, and admins can disable bypass and auto modes. No scheduled stop-control testing is published.

OVERSIGHT-2.evidence: Claude Code tool scope is set by per-project and managed allow, ask and deny rules; allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly makes managed settings the only rule source. Review on change is supported via ConfigChange hooks but not evidenced.

LOG-1.evidence: For Anthropic-hosted Claude Code cloud sessions, all operations are logged for compliance and audit purposes. Tamper-evident storage or retention periods for these logs are not stated publicly.

LOG-2.evidence: A Safeguards team and threat intelligence function detect misuse, build automated detections and ban accounts; the Sept 2026 report covers disruptions across seven harm areas, and enforcement data reports 11.4 million bans in H1 2026.

LOG-3.evidence: The RSP describes an incident response protocol and jailbreak rapid response; staff have an emergency alerting channel. Mapped reporting duties are exercised: 15,079 NCMEC reports in H1 2026 and IOC sharing with partners and governments.

SUPPLY-1.evidence: Vendors that handle Anthropic data must hold recognised certifications and undergo independent security audits. A public model inventory with re-review on provider change is not published.

TRANSP-1.evidence: Anthropic publishes a system card for each model (latest Haiku 5.5, Oct 2026) covering capabilities, safety evaluations and deployment decisions, and a Transparency Hub model report with training data, limitations and evaluation summaries.

EVAL-1.evidence: Models undergo RSP capability evaluations on a set interval plus internal and external red teaming; named external evaluators include UK AISI, US CAISI and METR. Results appear in system cards and Risk Reports.

CHANGE-1.evidence: Anthropic states it is implementing NIST SSDF and SLSA to create a chain of custody from a deployed model back to its developer, with two-party control on production systems. No attestation of change control over prompts or models was found.

APP-5.evidence: The Claude API enforces organisation-level rate limits (RPM, ITPM, OTPM) and monthly spend caps, and customers can set lower spend and rate limits per workspace. Spend alerting was not confirmed on the fetched page.

APP-7.evidence: Users can report harmful or inaccurate output via the in-product thumbs-down feature or usersafety@anthropic.com; security issues go through HackerOne with a three-business-day acknowledgement. Triage SLAs for output reports are not published.

AGENT-2.evidence: Claude Code tiers actions: read-only actions run freely, edits and shell commands need approval in Manual mode, and auto mode routes actions to a safety classifier. Docs acknowledge prompt fatigue; no audit of rubber-stamping is published.

AGENT-4.evidence: Claude Code cloud sessions run in isolated Anthropic-managed VMs with limited, allowlistable network access, credentials kept out of the VM, and VMs reclaimed after inactivity. The local bash sandbox is off by default.

MCP-1.evidence: By default users can add any MCP server; admins can enforce an exclusive managed-mcp.json set or an allowlist locked to managed settings in Claude Code. Usage of servers can be monitored via OpenTelemetry. Anthropic does not audit MCP servers.

MCP-8.evidence: Developer guidance says to deliver third-party content in tool results, which Claude treats skeptically; Claude Code gates actions with permission prompts. The Transparency Hub reports Sonnet 4.5 prevented 94% of prompt injection attacks via MCP.

MCP-9.evidence: Claude Code OpenTelemetry export can log tool calls with user email, account and session IDs, and MCP server and tool names when OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1. Telemetry and tool details are opt-in, not on by default.

EU-5.evidence: As a general-purpose model provider, Anthropic said in July 2025 it intends to sign the EU GPAI Code of Practice and publishes per-model training data descriptions and system cards. A copyright policy page was not verified.
